correctness.rationale: Private-zero chores must be assigned to their unique zero-cost owner by a strict Pareto-improving transfer; the resulting total cost u attains a fractional lower bound. Direct EFX checks for any removed owned item yield the stated inequalities including empty bundles. Multinomial counting gives the exact formula; two-agent intervals yield the parity result; the multinomial CLT, continuity of Gaussian range, Chebyshev/union bound, and fixed-width Stirling formula prove all asymptotic claims. The embedded standard-library checker independently enumerates 174 instances and 81,620 assignments and verifies 176 symmetric identities. Finite tests are corroboration, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact census and frequency of fair efficient outcomes are motivated by selecting and sampling among potentially many EFX+fPO solutions, beyond mere existence. The sharp nonmonotonicity of the count when one private zero-cost chore is added (half as many for all odd u, more for all even u) is a natural structural boundary, and sqrt(u) is the precise onset scale for EFX prevalence with symmetric private chores. The restriction is explicit; the counting and CLT arithmetic are not asserted to be independent probability-theory inventions.
